PoA M1: https://genwealth-56d653c6151d.herokuapp.com
Thanks for reviewing, in order to explain the features, let me explain something about the dApp design.
There are 2 types of keys, Vault Keys and Pocket Keys.
When you create a vault, you will get a Vault Key. This Vault Key allows you to access all the vault features, meaning that if you send this key token to another wallet then you're transferring your vault ownership to that other wallet.
When you create a pocket, you need to mint a Pocket Key and send it to your beneficiary. The idea is that you can do this at a later time so your beneficiaries can't see how much they'll get from the get-go. As a vault owner, you can also act as a beneficiary just for testing, so you can just mint a Pocket Key and send it to your own address. This Pocket Key allows the holder to redeem the contents of the corresponding when the vault deadline passes.
When the deadline for a vault passes, the vault is now in the unlocked state. Everyone holding the Pocket Keys will be able to redeem the assets from their corresponding pocket. But the Vault Key holder may still be able to postpone the deadline even though the vault has been unlocked to "re-lock" the vault. If during the unlocked period there are pocket redemptions, they cannot be reversed.
Now, to clear the questions about:
・Burn Pocket Key
・Vault Staking
・Pocket Deletion

Burn Pocket Key
In order to be able to burn a pocket key, you must hold a pocket key itself. There's no way to burn a key token residing in someone else's wallet without their signature. This feature is provided in the dApp just for the sake of completeness. Because in a typical scenario, the pocket keys are held by the beneficiaries, not the vault owner itself.
To burn a pocket key, select your desired pocket. Click the Mint Pocket Key button on the right sidebar, then go to the Burn tab. If you don't possess the corresponding pocket key, you will see: "Found no [POCKET_NAME] key in your wallet. Incorrect? R

ms.promise:
Public Testnet of the GenWealth Dapp of GenWealth. 
Using this Dapp you should be able to: 
Create Vault -> Here, the users can set-up the initial configurations of the vault, such as the vault name, initial deadline, and vault icon.
Create Pocket -> A pocket is a storage unit within a vault where the vault owner deposit their tokens. After the vault deadline passes, a beneficiary can redeem the contents of the pocket if they possess the corresponding pocket key.
Update Vault -> To postpone the deadline as well as renaming the vault.
Update Pocket -> This will allow the users to rename the pockets.
Mint and Burn Vault Keys -> As the name suggests, this is to mint and burn vault keys. The usage of vault keys is as described in Milestone 1.
Mint and Burn Pocket Keys -> As the name suggests, this is to mint and burn pocket keys. The usage of pocket keys is as described in Milestone 1.
Deposit and Withdraw -> These actions enables the vault owner to deposit and withdraw assets to the pockets.
Vault Staking -> This includes 4 actions: stake registration, pool delegation/redelegation, rewards withdrawal, and stake deregistration.
Pocket Deletion -> This is to delete a pocket.
